```{python}
import plotly.io as pio
pio.templates.default = "plotly_white"
import pandas as pd

skills_data = {
    "Name": ["Yasmine", "Wenjie", "Jinyi", "Yanyang"],
    "Python": [3, 4, 4, 4],
    "SQL": [4, 3, 4, 3],
    "Machine Learning": [3, 3, 3, 4],
    "Cloud Computing": [4, 4, 3, 3],
    "AWS": [4,4,4,4]
}

df_skills = pd.DataFrame(skills_data)
df_skills.set_index("Name", inplace=True)
df_skills
```

```{python}
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.set(style="white", font_scale=1.1)

ax = sns.heatmap(
    df_skills,
    annot=True,     
    cmap="coolwarm",    
    linewidths=1,    
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Skill Level'}, 
    square=True
)

plt.title("Team Skill  Heatmap", fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.yticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("figures/skillheatmap.png")
plt.show()

```

```{python}
from collections import Counter

# Assuming job_descriptions is a list of text from job postings
top_skills = ["Python", "SQL", "Machine Learning", "Cloud Computing", "Docker", "AWS"]
job_skill_counts = Counter(top_skills)

# Compare with team skill levels
for skill in top_skills:
    if skill not in df_skills.columns:
        df_skills[skill] = 0  # Assume no knowledge in missing skills

df_skills
```

The team shows strong skills in Python, SQL, machine learning, cloud computing, and AWS, but all members have a clear gap in Docker. Since no one currently has experience with Docker, this should be the main focus. Docker is widely used for deploying and managing applications, so learning how to use it will benefit the whole team. A good starting point is the official Docker “Get Started” guide. Each member can take on a different topic—like building images, running containers, or using Docker Compose—and teach it to the others in short sessions.

Besides Docker, each member has one or two areas to work on. Yasmine could improve her machine learning skills, and online courses like “Intro to Machine Learning” on Coursera would help. Wenjie can focus on SQL, using platforms like Mode Analytics to practice. Jinyi and Yanyang should strengthen their cloud computing knowledge further, especially by exploring AWS or GCP tutorials. To close the gap, the team can meet weekly to share what they’ve learned and apply new skills to a small joint project that includes Docker and cloud deployment. This hands-on work will help them grow and collaborate more effectively.
